issues.message: PMTUD black hole 10.1.1.10 -> 10.3.3.30: DF probes up to 1400 bytes answered, 3 probe(s) of 1500 bytes or more vanished with no ICMP Fragmentation Needed seen; path MTU is between 1400 and 1499

TCP black hole 10.3.3.30:80 -> 10.1.1.10:40100: 1 DF segment(s) of 1488+ bytes retransmitted and never acknowledged while segments up to 240 bytes were; no ICMP seen: lower the MSS (ip tcp adjust-mss) or let ICMP type 3 code 4 through

limits: Only what crossed this capture point is visible: a Fragmentation Needed sent towards a host on another segment, or dropped by an ACL before this point, is invisible here, so a black hole verdict means 'no ICMP seen here', not proof that no router sent one.
A vanished probe can be loss rather than MTU; the black hole verdict needs smaller probes to the same destination answered and larger ones never answered.
Fragments captured on one side of the reassembling host show whether pieces arrived here; whether the host reassembled them is not visible.
IPv6 extension headers (including fragment headers) are not decoded.
verdict: PMTUD black hole 10.1.1.10 -> 10.3.3.30 (path MTU between 1400 and 1499).
